title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: YOLANDA ON THE AIR
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Yolanda Price, night clerk at the Wagon Wheel Motel in Casper, Wyoming.
In September her son Danny joined the Navy. And her house got very, very quiet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DUSTY BOX
segments.quote: That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.
segments.author: Neil Armstrong
lines: One sleepless night she opened a box from her late grandpa. Inside was his old ham radio.
On the lid he had written what he heard on it in nineteen sixty-nine, from Neil Armstrong:
That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.
So Yolanda took one small step. She signed up for the license test.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE TEST
segments.quote: You may be disappointed if you fail, but you are doomed if you don't try.
segments.author: Beverly Sills
lines: She studied between check-ins. Then she failed by two questions.
She almost put the box back. Then she remembered the opera singer Beverly Sills:
You may be disappointed if you fail, but you are doomed if you don't try.
Three weeks later she passed. She told the ice machine first. Nobody else was awake.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE FIRST VOICE
segments.quote: Good communication is as stimulating as black coffee, and just as hard to sleep after.
segments.author: Anne Morrow Lindbergh
lines: For two weeks, only static. Then a raspy voice answered. Augie, eighty-four, a retired sponge diver in Florida.
They talked fishing and bad knees till four a.m. She thought of Anne Morrow Lindbergh:
Good communication is as stimulating as black coffee, and just as hard to sleep after.
So Augie got a standing date. Tuesdays at nine. She brought a thermos.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BLIZZARD
segments.quote: I would rather walk with a friend in the dark, than alone in the light.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: In December a blizzard closed the interstate. Phones died. Forty trucks were stuck.
On the radio she found Luis, a scared young driver alone in his cab. She thought of Helen Keller:
I would rather walk with a friend in the dark, than alone in the light.
So she stayed with him all night, until the plows came.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TEAM
segments.quote: It's when you know you're licked before you begin but you begin anyway and you see it through no matter what.
segments.author: Harper Lee
lines: Then the county asked her to start a storm radio team. Her license was five months old.
In Grandpa's old copy of To Kill a Mockingbird, she found a line he'd underlined:
It's when you know you're licked before you begin but you begin anyway and you see it through no matter what.
So she said yes. By spring she'd trained nine volunteers, including one grumpy dentist.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: CHRISTMAS EVE
segments.quote: In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.
segments.author: Albert Camus
lines: On Christmas Eve, Danny's ship was far out in the Pacific. Then the phone rang. Hi, Mom.
At nine, Augie came on the radio with his whole family, singing off-key. She thought of Albert Camus:
In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.
Outside, snow fell. Inside, Yolanda laughed until she cried.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Take a small step. Try again. Talk. Stay with a friend. Begin anyway. Find your summer.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Take one small step. Try again. Talk to someone. Stay with a friend. Begin anyway. And find your summer.
I tried ham radio once. The only person who answered was my wife, from the kitchen.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
